docs/agents/multi-agent-and-subagents.ht.title: Multi-Agent Teams & Subagents | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/agents/multi-agent-and-subagents.ht.summary: Multi-Agent Teams & Subagents Complex workflows often require dividing responsibilities across specialized agents. The MyAgents.Agents package provides hierarchical subagent dispatching, group chat coordination, and multi-model cost routing. 1. Hierarchical Subagent Dispatching A parent orchestrator agent can delegate tasks to specialized child subagents using HierarchicalSubagentDispatcher: flowchart TD User --> Parent[Lead Researcher Agent] Parent -->|invoke_subagent| Sub1[Web Search Subagent] Parent -->|invoke_subagent| Sub2[Data Analysis Subagent] Parent -->|invoke_subagent| Sub3[Code Writer Subagent] Sub1 --> Parent Sub2 --> Parent Sub3 --> Parent Configuring Subagents using MyAgents.Agents.Orchestration; var services = new ServiceCollection(); // Register subagent definitions services.AddSubagent("web-searcher", searcherDefinition); services.AddSubagent("data-analyst", analystDefinition); services.AddSubagent("code-writer", coderDefinition); // Add dispatcher and parent orchestration feature services.AddHierarchicalSubagents(options => { options.MaxSubagentTurns = 5; options.MaxParallelSubagents = 3; }); The parent agent automatically receives an invoke_subagent tool to spawn child tasks and collect their answers. 2. Multi-Agent Group Chat When multiple agents need to converse and collaborate in a shared thread, use GroupChat or SelectorGroupChat: using MyAgents.Agents; var group = new SelectorGroupChat( agents: [researcherAgent, reviewerAgent, writerAgent], managerChatClient: coordinatorChatClient, maxTurns: 10 ); var transcript = await group.RunAsync("Produce a technical brief on NativeAOT in .NET 10."); 3. Intelligent Model Cost Routing Large frontier models (e.g., GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) are expensive for routine classification or simple formatting tasks. Use MultiModelRoutingChatClient to route queries dynamically based on complexity, token budget, or prompt classification: using MyAgents.Agents.Routing; services.AddMultiModelRouting(options => { // Fast, inexpensive tier for simple turns options.RegisterTier(ModelTier.Economy, cheapClient, new ModelPricing(InputPerMillion: 0.15m, OutputPerMillion: 0.60m)); // Reasoning tier for complex tool calling and analysis options.RegisterTier(ModelTier.Reasoning, frontierClient, new ModelPricing(InputPerMillion: 5.00m, OutputPerMillion: 15.00m)); options.DailyCostBudgetUsd = 25.00m; });

docs/core/architecture.html.title: Architecture & Execution Lifecycle | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/core/architecture.html.summary: Architecture & Execution Lifecycle MyAgents Community is designed with a strict separation of concerns between agent definitions, runtime execution loops, tool invocation policies, and state persistence. Architecture Overview flowchart TD subgraph Client Application App[Host Application / Web API] Factory[IAgentSessionFactory] end subgraph Assembly & Definition Definition[AgentDefinition] Features[Feature Pipeline: Prompts, Tools, Capabilities] end subgraph Turn Execution Loop Session[IAgentSession] Runtime[MyAgents.Runtime.Chat] ChatClient[Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient] LLM[Model Provider: OpenAI, Ollama, Azure, etc.] end subgraph Governance & Tools Approval[IToolApprovalPolicy] ToolRegistry[ITool Catalog] NativeTools[NativeAOT Generated Tools] McpTools[Model Context Protocol Tools] DelegateTools[In-Process Delegate Tools] end App --> Factory Factory -->|Creates| Session Definition -->|Configures| Session Features -->|Contributes| Definition Session --> Runtime Runtime <--> ChatClient ChatClient <--> LLM Runtime --> Approval Approval -->|Approved| ToolRegistry ToolRegistry --> NativeTools ToolRegistry --> McpTools ToolRegistry --> DelegateTools Core Abstractions 1. AgentDefinition An immutable description of an agent's identity, metadata, and capabilities. Built modularly using IAgentFeature: var definition = new AgentDefinition("financial-analyst", [ new PromptRegistryFeature(...), new ToolApprovalFeature(policy), new RetrievalAugmentationFeature(retriever) ]); 2. IAgentFeature Features are the primary unit of extensibility. When an agent session initializes, every feature participates in an assembly phase to contribute: System Prompts: Injected into the prompt chain before model invocation. Tools: Registers available functions (ITool) with JSON schema descriptions. Context Augmentation: Intercepts turns before/after model requests (e.g. RAG, guardrails, memory). Tool Interception: Wraps tool executions to enforce policies, caching, or rate limits. 3. IAgentSessionFactory & IAgentSession IAgentSessionFactory is registered in Microsoft Dependency Injection and manufactures IAgentSession instances. Each IAgentSession represents an active conversation. Maintains isolated message history. Disposes resources cleanly when the conversation finishes (IAsyncDisposable). The Turn Execution Lifecycle When session.InvokeAsync(messages) or session.InvokeStreamingAsync(messages) is called: sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User participant Session as IAgentSession participant Feature as Feature Pipeline participant Runtime as ChatRuntime participant LLM as IChatClient participant Policy as IToolApprovalPolicy participant Tool as ITool User->>Session: InvokeAsync(messages) Session->>Feature: AugmentContextAsync(context) Feature-->>Session: Augmented Context Session->>Runtime: ExecuteTurnAsync(context) loop Model & Tool Loop Runtime->>LLM: GetResponseAsync(history, tools) LLM-->>Runtime: ChatResponse (ToolCall request) Runtime->>Policy: EvaluateAsync(toolCall) alt Approved Policy-->>Runtime: Allow Runtime->>Tool: InvokeAsync(arguments) Tool-->>Runtime: ToolResult Runtime->>Runtime: Append ToolResult to history else Rejected / Requires Human Policy-->>Runtime: Reject / Wait Runtime->>Runtime: Handle Rejection or Pause end end Runtime-->>Session: Final AgentTurnResult Session-->>User: Output Messages Context Augmentation: Any registered features (e.g. memory retrieval, guardrails) augment input messages. Model Request: The ChatRuntime serializes messages and tool schemas to IChatClient. Tool Call Detection: If the model requests one or more tool calls, the runtime parses the request. Approval Check: Before executing any tool, IToolApprovalPolicy verifies the tool name and arguments. Tool Execution: Approved tools execute asynchronously with cancellation token support. Result Feedback: Tool outputs are formatted as tool messages and sent back to the model. Completion: When the model finishes generating its final response, the turn completes and returns AgentTurnResult.

docs/core/sessions-and-turns.html.title: Sessions & Turns | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/core/sessions-and-turns.html.summary: Sessions & Turns An agent interaction in MyAgents Community consists of Sessions and Turns. Understanding Sessions An IAgentSession manages an ongoing conversation between a user and an agent. It provides: Isolated State: Conversation history, variables, and session-owned resources. Resource Lifetime: Any tools or connections opened during a session (such as local MCP child processes or database connections) are automatically disposed when the session is disposed. Turn Invocation: Synchronous and streaming invocation methods. Creating a Session using MyAgents.Core; // Resolve the session factory from DI var factory = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); // Create a named session with a specific definition await using var session = factory.CreateSession("user-1001-conversation", definition); Executing Conversational Turns A turn represents a single input/output cycle: the user supplies one or more messages, and the agent processes them (including zero or more tool calls) to produce an output. Standard Invocation (InvokeAsync) Use InvokeAsync when you want the complete final response once all tool calls and reasoning steps are finished: var input = AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Summarize our quarterly metrics."); AgentTurnResult turn = await session.InvokeAsync([input], cancellationToken); foreach (var message in turn.Output) { Console.WriteLine($"[{message.Role}]: {message.Content}"); } Streaming Invocation (InvokeStreamingAsync) Use InvokeStreamingAsync for low-latency interactive applications (like chat web UIs or CLI spinners) where tokens should be rendered as they arrive: var input = AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Draft an email to the engineering team."); await foreach (AgentTurnResult update in session.InvokeStreamingAsync([input], cancellationToken)) { foreach (var message in update.Output) { Console.Write(message.Content); } } Console.WriteLine(); Tip Even during streaming, MyAgents Community maintains strict tool approval safety. If a tool requires human approval or triggers a policy rejection, the stream handles the pause/rejection cleanly before continuing. Session Messages & Roles MyAgents Community uses strongly-typed AgentMessage records with standard roles: AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Hello!"): User prompt. AgentMessage.FromText("assistant", "How can I help?"): Model output. AgentMessage.FromText("system", "Instructions here."): System prompt. AgentMessage.FromToolResult(toolCallId, "42"): Tool execution result payload. Session History & Trimming To prevent sessions from exceeding LLM context windows in long-running conversations, you can register a ContextWindowFeature: using MyAgents.Agents; var definition = new AgentDefinition("chat-agent", [ new ContextWindowFeature(new ContextWindowOptions { MaxTokens = 8000, PreserveSystemPrompt = true, KeepLatestUserMessages = 4 }) ]);

docs/execution/durable-runs.html.title: Durable Agent Runs | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/execution/durable-runs.html.summary: Durable Agent Runs MyAgents.Runtime.Workers and MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite provide a durable, asynchronous task execution engine for long-running agent workloads. Why Durable Runs? In production, agents often execute complex, multi-minute tasks such as crawling web pages, ingesting datasets, or conducting multi-step research. Running these inside a standard HTTP request is brittle: Server deployments or container restarts kill in-flight requests. Transient network drops cause duplicate agent executions. Load spikes can overwhelm LLM provider rate limits. Durable Runs decouple submission from execution using a lease-based background worker pool. Architecture flowchart TD subgraph Submission Client[Web API / CLI] -->|SubmitAsync| Backend[IAgentRunBackend (Sqlite)] Backend -->|Write Pending Record| Table[(Persistent Runs Store)] end subgraph Worker Pool WorkerService[AgentRunWorkerService] -->|TryAcquireLeaseAsync| Table Table -->|Leased to Worker 1| WorkerService WorkerService -->|Heartbeat Renewal| Table WorkerService -->|Execute| Handler[IAgentRunHandler] Handler -->|Output Result| Result[AgentRunHandlerResult] Result -->|Mark Completed / Failed| Table end 1. Configuring the Durable Worker Host Configure your background service using standard .NET Generic Host: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting; using MyAgents.Core.Execution; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers; using MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite; var builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder(); // 1. Register SQLite persistence backend builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAgentRunBackend>(_ => new SqliteAgentRunBackend("agent-runs.db")); // 2. Register your custom run handler builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAgentRunHandler, DataProcessingAgentHandler>(); // 3. Register the durable worker service builder.Services.AddMyAgentsRunWorker(options => { options.IdlePollInterval = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(250); options.LeaseDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30); options.LeaseRenewalInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10); options.BaseRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2); options.MaximumRetryDelay = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5); }); using var host = builder.Build(); await host.RunAsync(); 2. Implementing IAgentRunHandler A run handler executes the actual business logic for an agent run: public sealed class DataProcessingAgentHandler : IAgentRunHandler { private readonly IAgentSessionFactory _sessionFactory; public DataProcessingAgentHandler(IAgentSessionFactory sessionFactory) { _sessionFactory = sessionFactory; } public async ValueTask<AgentRunHandlerResult> HandleAsync( AgentRunContext context, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { // Create an isolated session for this durable run await using var session = _sessionFactory.CreateSession(context.RunId, MyAgentDefinitions.Default); var userMessage = AgentMessage.FromText("user", context.InputJson); var result = await session.InvokeAsync([userMessage], cancellationToken); return AgentRunHandlerResult.Completed(result.Output.Last().Content); } } 3. Submitting Runs with Idempotency Submissions are resilient to duplicate calls: var backend = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IAgentRunBackend>(); var request = new AgentRunRequest( HandlerId: "data-processing", InputJson: """{"dataset": "sales-q3", "action": "audit"}""", IdempotencyKey: "sales-q3-audit-2026", ScopeKey: "tenant-acme" ); var submission = await backend.SubmitAsync(request, cancellationToken); if (submission.WasDeduplicated) { Console.WriteLine($"Duplicate request detected. Returning existing RunId: {submission.RunId}"); } else { Console.WriteLine($"New Run enqueued: {submission.RunId}"); } Crash Recovery & Lease Management Lease Acquisition: A worker acquires a lease on a run with an expiration timestamp (LeaseExpiresAt). Heartbeats: While processing, the worker automatically renews its lease every LeaseRenewalInterval. Automatic Recovery: If the host process is killed or panics, the lease expires. Another worker claims the expired lease, increments the attempt count, and retries or resumes execution.

docs/getting-started/packages.html.title: Package Ecosystem | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/getting-started/packages.html.summary: Package Ecosystem MyAgents Community is built as a set of modular, decoupled NuGet packages for .NET 10. Install only what your application requires. Core Packages Matrix Package Version Description Target Use Case MyAgents.Core 1.0.0 Core abstractions: IAgent, AgentDefinition, IAgentSession, ITool, messages, and prompts. Included in all applications. MyAgents.Runtime.Chat 1.0.0 Provider-neutral conversational runtime integrating with Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient. Interactive chat applications, CLI bots, web APIs. MyAgents.Generators 1.0.0 Roslyn incremental source generator for [AgentTool] compile-time tool binding. High-performance and NativeAOT trimmed applications. MyAgents.Memory 1.0.0 SIMD dense vector similarity (TensorPrimitives), BM25 sparse index, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, document readers. In-memory RAG, semantic search, long-term memory. MyAgents.Runtime.Workers 1.0.0 Durable background worker host with lease coordination, idempotency, and retries. Long-running asynchronous workflows, background task queues. MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite 1.0.0 SQLite-backed persistent run backend for durable worker execution. On-premises and single-node durable worker storage. MyAgents.Mcp 1.0.0 Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool adapters for stdio and HTTP/SSE transports. Connecting to local or remote MCP servers and tools. MyAgents.Agents 1.0.0 High-level orchestrations: subagents, group chat, token cost tracking, and model routing. Complex multi-agent teams, hierarchical delegation. MyAgents.Testing 1.0.0 In-memory test runtime, deterministic mock agents, and turn assertions. Unit tests and integration test suites. Installation Commands Conversational Chat Agent dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat High-Performance NativeAOT Agent with Compile-Time Tools dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Generators Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Memory Durable Worker Process (Background Queue) dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Workers dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite External MCP Tools Integration dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Mcp Multi-Agent Workflows & Cost Routing dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package MyAgents.Agents Unit Testing Suite dotnet add package MyAgents.Testing

docs/getting-started/quickstart.html.title: Quick Start Guide | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/getting-started/quickstart.html.summary: Quick Start Guide In this guide, you will build and run your first tool-calling AI agent using MyAgents Community in under 5 minutes. Prerequisites .NET 10 SDK An API key for an LLM provider (e.g., OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, or Anthropic) or an in-memory mock client. 1. Create a New Console Application dotnet new console -n MyFirstAgent cd MyFirstAgent 2. Add Required NuGet Packages Install the core abstractions, chat runtime, and your preferred AI client: dotnet add package MyAgents.Core dotnet add package MyAgents.Runtime.Chat dotnet add package Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI Note MyAgents Community is completely provider-neutral. It interfaces directly with any Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient implementation (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Ollama, GitHub Models, AWS Bedrock, etc.). 3. Build Your First Agent Replace Program.cs with the following code: using System.ComponentModel; using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; using MyAgents.Runtime.Chat; using OpenAI; // 1. Configure the AI Chat Client var apiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("OPENAI_API_KEY") ?? "your-api-key"; var chatClient = new OpenAIClient(apiKey).GetChatClient("gpt-4o-mini"); // 2. Register MyAgents runtime in Dependency Injection var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>(chatClient); services.AddMyAgentsChatRuntime(); await using var serviceProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var sessionFactory = serviceProvider.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); // 3. Define the Agent and its capabilities var weatherTool = DelegateTool.Create( name: "get_weather", description: "Gets the current temperature and conditions for a given city.", handler: ([Description("The city name")] string city) => { return $"Weather in {city}: 21°C (70°F), Clear Skies"; }); var definition = new AgentDefinition("weather-assistant", [ AgentFeature.Create(assembly => { assembly.Prompts.AddSystem("You are a concise, helpful assistant. Always use tools to answer weather queries."); assembly.Tools.Add(weatherTool); }) ]); // 4. Create an isolated conversation session await using var session = sessionFactory.CreateSession("session-demo-1", definition); // 5. Invoke the agent Console.WriteLine("User: What's the weather in Vancouver?"); var result = await session.InvokeAsync([ AgentMessage.FromText("user", "What's the weather in Vancouver?") ]); // 6. Display the assistant's response foreach (var message in result.Output) { Console.WriteLine($"Assistant: {message.Content}"); } 4. Run the Application dotnet run Expected Output User: What's the weather in Vancouver? Assistant: The current weather in Vancouver is 21°C (70°F) with clear skies. Next Steps Explore Package Ecosystem to discover additional modules like RAG, background workers, and source generators. Learn about NativeAOT Tools for compile-time reflection-free performance. Learn about Durable Runs for crash-resilient background processing.

docs/governance/circuit-breakers.html.title: Circuit Breakers & Observability | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/governance/circuit-breakers.html.summary: Circuit Breakers & Observability To protect downstream services from runaway loops, sudden model hallucinations, and cascading failures, MyAgents Community provides built-in circuit breakers, execution observers, and OpenTelemetry metrics. 1. Tool Circuit Breaker When an external tool dependency fails repeatedly (e.g. database timeout or third-party API outage), the CircuitBreakerMiddleware trips open, immediately rejecting further tool calls before they hit the failing service: using MyAgents.Core.Middleware; var circuitBreaker = new CircuitBreakerMiddleware(new CircuitBreakerOptions { FailureThreshold = 3, // Trip after 3 consecutive failures BreakDuration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30), // Stay open for 30 seconds HandledExceptions = [typeof(HttpRequestException), typeof(TimeoutException)] }); When tripped, the circuit breaker returns a structured error to the model so the agent can adapt or inform the user rather than hanging. 2. Tool Observers Tool observers allow you to audit, log, or measure tool execution without altering the tool's business logic: using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed class SecurityAuditToolObserver : IToolObserver { private readonly ILogger _logger; public SecurityAuditToolObserver(ILogger logger) { _logger = logger; } public void OnToolInvoking(ToolInvokingContext context) { _logger.LogInformation("Tool {ToolName} invoking with args: {Args}", context.ToolName, context.ArgumentsJson); } public void OnToolInvoked(ToolInvokedContext context) { _logger.LogInformation("Tool {ToolName} completed in {ElapsedMs}ms. Success: {IsSuccess}", context.ToolName, context.Duration.TotalMilliseconds, context.Result.IsSuccess); } } Register observers using ToolObserverFeature: var definition = new AgentDefinition("audited-agent", [ new ToolObserverFeature(new SecurityAuditToolObserver(logger)) ]); 3. OpenTelemetry Metrics & Tracing MyAgents.Agents integrates natively with System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource and OpenTelemetry: services.AddOpenTelemetry() .WithTracing(tracing => { tracing.AddSource("MyAgents.Community"); tracing.AddOtlpExporter(); }) .WithMetrics(metrics => { metrics.AddMeter("MyAgents.Community"); metrics.AddOtlpExporter(); }); Exported metrics include: agent.turn.duration_ms: Duration of conversational turns. agent.tool.invocations_total: Counter of tool calls tagged by tool name and status. agent.tokens.cost_usd: Real-time token usage and cost metrics per model tier.

docs/governance/tool-approval.html.title: Tool Approval & Allowlisting | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/governance/tool-approval.html.summary: Tool Approval & Allowlisting When AI agents execute tools that write to production databases, send emails, or charge credit cards, safety policies are required to prevent unintended actions. The IToolApprovalPolicy Interface Every tool call generated by a model passes through an IToolApprovalPolicy before the tool handler is executed: flowchart LR Model[Model requests tool call] --> Policy[IToolApprovalPolicy] Policy -->|Allow| Exec[Execute Tool] Policy -->|RequiresApproval| Human[Human-in-the-Loop Gate] Policy -->|Reject| Error[Return Rejection Message to Model] 1. Configuring Rule-Based Allowlisting You can configure granular allowlists and rejection rules using RuleBasedToolApprovalPolicy: using MyAgents.Core.Approvals; var policy = new RuleBasedToolApprovalPolicy() // 1. Safe read-only tools execute without prompting .AllowTool("get_current_time") .AllowTool("search_knowledge_base") .AllowToolPrefix("read_") // 2. Sensitive tools require human supervisor approval .RequireApproval("delete_customer_account") .RequireApproval("execute_wire_transfer") // 3. Reject any unknown tool by default .SetDefaultDecision(ToolApprovalDecision.Reject( reason: "policy_violation", message: "Tool is not in the approved corporate allowlist.")); 2. Implementing Human-in-the-Loop Gates When a tool decision is RequiresApproval, the runtime invokes an IToolApprovalGate to prompt a human operator or query an external authorization webhook: public sealed class ConsoleApprovalGate : IToolApprovalGate { public ValueTask<bool> RequestApprovalAsync( ToolApprovalRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { Console.ForegroundColor = ConsoleColor.Yellow; Console.WriteLine($"\n[SECURITY ALERT] Agent wants to call: {request.ToolName}"); Console.WriteLine($"Arguments: {request.ArgumentsJson}"); Console.Write("Approve execution? (y/n): "); Console.ResetColor(); var response = Console.ReadLine(); return ValueTask.FromResult(string.Equals(response?.Trim(), "y", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)); } } Register the gate in your agent definition: var definition = new AgentDefinition("guarded-agent", [ new ToolApprovalFeature(policy, new ConsoleApprovalGate()) ]);

docs/memory/document-ingestion.html.title: Document Ingestion & Chunking | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/memory/document-ingestion.html.summary: Document Ingestion & Chunking The MyAgents.Memory package includes built-in document readers and chunkers that ingest structured and unstructured files with zero external parsing dependencies. Supported Document Formats Markdown (.md): Preserves heading hierarchy (#, ##, ###), list items, and code blocks. HTML (.html, .htm): Extracts title tags, removes navigation/script boilerplates, and strips tags while preserving structure. Plain Text (.txt): Splits text with sentence-boundary and paragraph awareness. JSON (.json): Splits JSON objects or array elements into discrete searchable records. 1. Registering Document Ingestion using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Memory.Ingestion; var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddDocumentIngestion(builder => { // Configure default chunk size and overlap in tokens/characters builder.WithChunkingOptions(new TextChunkingOptions( ChunkSize: 1000, ChunkOverlap: 100, PreserveHeadings: true)); // Register format-specific chunkers builder.UseMarkdownChunker(); builder.UseHtmlChunker(); builder.UsePlainTextChunker(); }); var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var ingestor = provider.GetRequiredService<IDocumentIngestor>(); 2. Ingesting Files and Streams Ingest a Local File var result = await ingestor.IngestFileAsync( filePath: "docs/architecture.md", targetNamespace: "project-knowledge", metadata: new Dictionary<string, string> { ["author"] = "Platform Team", ["version"] = "1.0.0" }, cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Ingested {result.DocumentId} into {result.ChunkCount} chunks."); Ingest an In-Memory Stream using var stream = File.OpenRead("webpage.html"); var result = await ingestor.IngestStreamAsync( stream: stream, contentType: "text/html", documentId: "release-notes-v1", targetNamespace: "project-knowledge", cancellationToken: cancellationToken); 3. Chunking Strategies The chunker automatically guarantees that chunks respect natural content boundaries: Markdown chunking never splits inside a fenced code block (```). Heading paths (# Guide > ## Architecture) are prepended to each chunk as context metadata to improve semantic search relevance. Token counts are calculated accurately without requiring heavyweight native tokenizers.

docs/memory/episodic-memory.html.title: Episodic Memory & Long-Term Recall | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/memory/episodic-memory.html.summary: Episodic Memory & Long-Term Recall While standard session state is ephemeral, real-world agents require long-term episodic memory to remember user preferences, previous decisions, and domain facts across different sessions and days. What is Episodic Memory? MyAgents.Memory provides IEpisodicMemoryStore, a high-level memory layer built on top of hybrid retrieval: Semantic Persistence: Automatically indexes conversational facts into a persistent store. Cross-Session Recall: Queries relevant memories based on conversational context. Automated Milestone Consolidation: Summarizes multiple related memories into concise milestone entries. Retention Policies: Trims expired or low-importance memories to respect token budgets. 1. Setting up Episodic Memory using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Memory; var services = new ServiceCollection(); // Registers IEpisodicMemoryStore and EpisodicMemoryFeature services.AddEpisodicMemory(ns: "user-longterm-memory"); var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var episodicStore = provider.GetRequiredService<IEpisodicMemoryStore>(); 2. Using the Episodic Memory Feature in an Agent Register EpisodicMemoryFeature in your agent definition to give the model tools to remember and recall information autonomously: var episodicFeature = provider.GetRequiredService<EpisodicMemoryFeature>(); var definition = new AgentDefinition("personal-assistant", [ episodicFeature ]); The feature automatically injects two tools into the model: remember(key, content, importance): Stores an episodic observation. recall(query, maxResults): Searches episodic memory for relevant facts. 3. Retention Policies & Summarization Over months of usage, memories accumulate. Use MemoryRetentionService to prune older memories while preserving summaries: var retentionService = provider.GetRequiredService<MemoryRetentionService>(); var policy = new MemoryRetentionPolicy( MaxEntries: 500, MaxAge: TimeSpan.FromDays(90), SummarizeTrimmedEntries: true, SummarySourceCount: 20, SummaryKeyPrefix: "milestone-summary" ); MemoryRetentionResult result = await retentionService.ApplyAsync( ns: "user-longterm-memory", policy: policy, cancellationToken: cancellationToken); Console.WriteLine($"Pruned {result.DeletedCount} entries, summarized {result.SummarizedCount} milestones.");

docs/memory/hybrid-rag.html.title: Hybrid RAG & Memory Retrieval | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/memory/hybrid-rag.html.summary: Hybrid RAG & Memory Retrieval MyAgents.Memory delivers an enterprise-grade retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system with zero external vector database dependencies. Why Hybrid Retrieval? Pure vector search (dense embeddings) excels at semantic understanding and conceptual matches, but struggles with exact identifiers, SKU numbers, code keywords, or rare terminology. Pure keyword search (BM25) excels at exact matches but lacks semantic awareness. MyAgents Community combines both using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): flowchart TD Query[User Query: 'NativeAOT source generator'] --> Dense[Dense Vector Search] Query --> Sparse[BM25 Lexical Search] Dense -->|TensorPrimitives.Dot SIMD| DenseRanks[Dense Ranked List] Sparse -->|Inverted Index TF-IDF| SparseRanks[Sparse Ranked List] DenseRanks --> RRF[Reciprocal Rank Fusion] SparseRanks --> RRF RRF --> FusedResults[Fused Grounded Context Results] 1. Configuring Hybrid Memory using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Memory; var services = new ServiceCollection(); // Register your embedding generator (e.g. OpenAI or local ONNX) services.AddSingleton<IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>>(embeddingGenerator); // Register in-memory or SQLite vector store services.AddSingleton<IMemoryStore, SqliteMemoryStore>(sp => new SqliteMemoryStore("vectors.db", sp.GetRequiredService<IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>>())); // Add Hybrid Memory Retrieval with BM25 indexing services.AddHybridMemoryRetrieval(); var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var retriever = provider.GetRequiredService<IHybridMemoryRetriever>(); 2. Executing a Hybrid Query var query = new HybridMemoryQuery( QueryText: "NativeAOT source generator", MaxResults: 5, RankingMode: HybridRankingMode.ReciprocalRankFusion, DenseWeight: 0.5, SparseWeight: 0.5, RrfK: 60 ); IReadOnlyList<HybridMemorySearchResult> results = await retriever.SearchHybridAsync( ns: "technical-docs", query: query, cancellationToken: cancellationToken); foreach (var hit in results) { Console.WriteLine($"[Score: {hit.FusedScore:F4}] {hit.Entry.Key}: {hit.Entry.Content}"); } 3. Grounded Citation Feature Inject retrieved context directly into the agent prompt with automatic citation markers ([1], [2]): var ragOptions = new RetrievalAugmentationOptions { MaxResults = 5, MaxContextTokens = 2000, AdjacentChunkWindow = 1, AppendCitationReferences = true }; var definition = new AgentDefinition("grounded-assistant", [ new RetrievalAugmentationFeature(retriever, ragOptions) ]);

docs/testing/testing-agents.html.title: Unit Testing Agents | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/testing/testing-agents.html.summary: Unit Testing Agents Testing conversational AI applications can be challenging because real LLM API calls are nondeterministic, slow, and incur token costs. The MyAgents.Testing package provides deterministic, in-memory mocks for testing agent definitions, prompt templates, and tool pipelines without hitting external APIs. Installation dotnet add package MyAgents.Testing 1. Using InMemoryAgent InMemoryAgent is a deterministic mock agent that returns pre-queued responses and records all incoming turn contexts: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Testing; using Xunit; public sealed class AgentWorkflowTests { [Fact] public async Task Agent_Returns_Expected_Sequence() { // 1. Arrange a mock agent with queued responses var mockAgent = new InMemoryAgent("MockReviewer") .EnqueueResponse("Step 1: Code verified.") .EnqueueResponse("Step 2: Ready for production."); var context1 = new AgentTurnContext("session-1", [AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Check PR #42")]); var context2 = new AgentTurnContext("session-1", [AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Proceed?")]); // 2. Act var result1 = await mockAgent.InvokeAsync(context1); var result2 = await mockAgent.InvokeAsync(context2); // 3. Assert Assert.Equal("Step 1: Code verified.", result1.Output[0].Content); Assert.Equal("Step 2: Ready for production.", result2.Output[0].Content); Assert.Equal(2, mockAgent.InvocationCount); } } 2. Testing with InMemoryAgentRuntime To test the entire session and feature pipeline (including tool execution and feature interceptors) with a fake model backend: using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Testing; using Xunit; public sealed class SessionTurnTests { [Fact] public async Task Session_Applies_SystemPrompts_And_Tools() { var runtime = new InMemoryAgentRuntime(); runtime.SetModelResponse("The current weather is sunny."); var definition = new AgentDefinition("assistant", [ AgentFeature.Create(assembly => { assembly.Prompts.AddSystem("You are a helpful assistant."); }) ]); var session = runtime.CreateSession("test-session", definition); var turnResult = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", "Hello")]); Assert.Equal("The current weather is sunny.", turnResult.Output[0].Content); } } 3. Testing Durable Run Handlers Use InMemoryAgentRunBackend to test durable worker handlers without spinning up a real SQLite database file: [Fact] public async Task DurableRun_Deduplicates_Duplicate_Keys() { var backend = new InMemoryAgentRunBackend(); var request = new AgentRunRequest( HandlerId: "report-generator", InputJson: "{}", IdempotencyKey: "unique-key-101"); var firstSubmission = await backend.SubmitAsync(request); var secondSubmission = await backend.SubmitAsync(request); Assert.False(firstSubmission.WasDeduplicated); Assert.True(secondSubmission.WasDeduplicated); Assert.Equal(firstSubmission.RunId, secondSubmission.RunId); }

docs/tools/delegate-tools.html.title: Delegate Tools & Custom Tools | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tools/delegate-tools.html.summary: Delegate Tools & Custom Tools In addition to compile-time source generated tools, MyAgents Community allows you to define dynamic in-process tools using DelegateTool or implement the ITool interface directly. Using DelegateTool DelegateTool is the fastest way to expose existing C# lambdas or methods as tools: using System.ComponentModel; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; // Parameterless tool var timeTool = DelegateTool.Create( name: "get_current_utc_time", description: "Returns the current UTC date and time in ISO 8601 format.", handler: () => DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToString("O") ); // Tool with parameters and descriptions var calculatorTool = DelegateTool.Create( name: "calculate_tax", description: "Calculates total price after tax.", handler: ( [Description("Subtotal in dollars")] decimal subtotal, [Description("Tax rate percentage (e.g. 0.05 for 5%)")] decimal taxRate) => { var tax = subtotal * taxRate; return new { Subtotal = subtotal, Tax = tax, Total = subtotal + tax }; } ); Async Handlers and Cancellation Tokens Delegate tools support asynchronous methods and automatically receive a CancellationToken: var searchTool = DelegateTool.Create( name: "query_database", description: "Queries the customer database asynchronously.", handler: async (string query, CancellationToken ct) => { return await myDbService.ExecuteQueryAsync(query, ct); } ); Implementing ITool Directly For complex stateful tools or reusable tool libraries, implement ITool: using System.Text.Json; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed class DatabaseQueryTool : ITool { public string Name => "execute_sql"; public string Description => "Executes a read-only SQL query against the analytics database."; public string ParametersSchemaJson => """ { "type": "object", "properties": { "sql": { "type": "string", "description": "The read-only SELECT query" } }, "required": ["sql"] } """; private readonly DbConnection _connection; public DatabaseQueryTool(DbConnection connection) { _connection = connection; } public async ValueTask<ToolExecutionResult> InvokeAsync( string argumentsJson, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(argumentsJson); var sql = doc.RootElement.GetProperty("sql").GetString(); var result = await _connection.QueryAsync(sql, cancellationToken); return ToolExecutionResult.Success(JsonSerializer.Serialize(result)); } } Tool Categories and Tags You can tag tools to group them for permission policies or telemetry: assembly.Tools.Add(timeTool); assembly.Tools.Add(calculatorTool);

docs/tools/mcp.html.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tools/mcp.html.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration The MyAgents.Mcp package provides first-class integration with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing your agents to interact with external tools and resources running over standard I/O (stdio) or HTTP/Server-Sent Events (SSE). Installation dotnet add package MyAgents.Mcp How MCP Works with MyAgents When you register an McpFeature on an AgentDefinition, the runtime connects to the target MCP server, queries its tool catalog, and translates them into ITool implementations: flowchart LR Agent[Agent Session] --> McpFeature[MyAgents.Mcp.McpFeature] McpFeature --> Client[McpClient] Client -->|Stdio or HTTP Transport| McpServer[External MCP Server] McpServer --> Tools[External Tools & Resources] 1. Local Process MCP Server (Stdio) To connect to a local MCP server running as a sub-process (e.g. SQLite, GitHub, or Filesystem MCP servers): using ModelContextProtocol.Client; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Mcp; // Configure stdio transport to launch a local server process var transport = new StdioClientTransport(new StdioClientTransportOptions { Command = "npx", Arguments = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite", "--db-path", "analytics.db"] }); var mcpFeature = new McpFeature(transport, new McpFeatureOptions { ImportPrompts = true, ExposeResourceTools = true }); var definition = new AgentDefinition("data-agent", [mcpFeature]); 2. Remote MCP Server (HTTP / SSE) To connect to a remote or containerized MCP server over HTTP / SSE: using ModelContextProtocol.Client; using MyAgents.Mcp; var httpTransport = new HttpClientTransport(new HttpClientTransportOptions { Endpoint = new Uri("https://mcp.internal.corp/sse") }); var mcpFeature = new McpFeature(httpTransport); var definition = new AgentDefinition("cloud-agent", [mcpFeature]); Multi-Server Aggregation If your agent requires tools from multiple different MCP servers simultaneously (e.g., both a GitHub MCP server and a Database MCP server), use McpMultiServerFeature: using MyAgents.Mcp; var multiServer = new McpMultiServerFeature(); multiServer.AddServer("db", new StdioClientTransport(new StdioClientTransportOptions { Command = "npx", Arguments = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sqlite", "app.db"] })); multiServer.AddServer("filesystem", new StdioClientTransport(new StdioClientTransportOptions { Command = "npx", Arguments = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/allowed/workspace"] })); var definition = new AgentDefinition("poly-agent", [multiServer]); Lifecycle & Session Ownership The underlying MCP connection and child process resources are owned by the active IAgentSession. When await session.DisposeAsync() is called at the end of a conversation, all child processes and connections are gracefully terminated.

docs/tools/nativeaot-tools.html.title: NativeAOT Compile-Time Tools | MyAgents Community Documentation
docs/tools/nativeaot-tools.html.summary: NativeAOT Compile-Time Tools The MyAgents.Generators package provides a Roslyn incremental source generator that translates C# methods marked with [AgentTool] into zero-reflection, compile-time tool bindings. Why Compile-Time Tools? Traditional agent frameworks rely on runtime reflection and System.Text.Json runtime schema generation to discover method signatures, serialize parameters, and invoke functions. In modern cloud, serverless, and edge environments, runtime reflection introduces: Trimming and NativeAOT Incompatibility: Reflection-based serializers risk trimming warnings or runtime crashes when compiled with PublishAot=true. Cold Start Latency: Reflection and JIT overhead add latency to the first tool execution. Allocation Overhead: Dynamic method invocation allocates on every call. MyAgents.Generators solves this by emitting: Fully static ITool classes. Compile-time constant strings for ParametersSchemaJson. Strongly-typed JSON context bindings. Authoring an [AgentTool] 1. Define Request and Response Models Ensure types are serializable via System.Text.Json: using System.ComponentModel; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; public sealed record CustomerInfoRequest( [Description("The unique customer ID")] string CustomerId); public sealed record CustomerInfoResponse( string Name, string Tier, int OpenTickets); [JsonSerializable(typeof(CustomerInfoRequest))] [JsonSerializable(typeof(CustomerInfoResponse))] internal sealed partial class CustomerJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext; 2. Implement the Tool Method Annotate a static or instance method with [AgentTool]: public static class CustomerServiceTools { [AgentTool( Description = "Retrieves account tier and open ticket counts for a customer.", JsonContext = typeof(CustomerJsonContext))] public static CustomerInfoResponse GetCustomerInfo(CustomerInfoRequest request) { return new CustomerInfoResponse( Name: "Acme Corp", Tier: "Enterprise", OpenTickets: 2); } } 3. Register the Generated Tool The source generator automatically creates an extension method AsGetCustomerInfoTool(): var definition = new AgentDefinition("support-agent", [ AgentFeature.Create(assembly => { // Add the generated compile-time tool assembly.Tools.Add(CustomerServiceToolsAgentToolsExtensions.AsGetCustomerInfoTool()); }) ]); Performance & Trimming Verification Because the generated code references CustomerJsonContext directly, the .NET trimming analyzer detects that all types are statically known: <PropertyGroup> <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> <EnableTrimAnalyzer>true</EnableTrimAnalyzer> </PropertyGroup> When building with dotnet publish -c Release, the compilation completes with 0 trim warnings and 0 AOT warnings.

index.html.title: MyAgents Community | MyAgents Community Documentation
index.html.summary: MyAgents Community Modular, NativeAOT-ready, and provider-neutral AI agent runtime for .NET 10. MyAgents Community is an enterprise-grade agent framework for .NET 10 built on top of Microsoft.Extensions.AI. It provides complete provider neutrality, compile-time NativeAOT tool generation, restart-recoverable durable worker execution, and hybrid RAG memory with zero vendor lock-in. 🚀 NativeAOT Ready Generate compile-time tool schemas and bindings with MyAgents.Generators. Zero runtime reflection, zero trimming warnings, and near-instant cold starts. Read NativeAOT Guide → 🛡️ Durable Execution Background worker leasing, idempotency deduplication, and automatic crash recovery with SQLite persistence via MyAgents.Runtime.Workers. Read Durable Runs → 🔍 Hybrid RAG Memory Fused SIMD dense cosine similarity (TensorPrimitives) and BM25 sparse lexical ranking with zero external vector database dependencies. Read Hybrid RAG → Quick Start (C#) using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection; using MyAgents.Core; using MyAgents.Core.Tools; using MyAgents.Runtime.Chat; // 1. Configure services with your IChatClient and MyAgents runtime var services = new ServiceCollection(); services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>(chatClient); services.AddMyAgentsChatRuntime(); await using var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider(); var sessionFactory = provider.GetRequiredService<IAgentSessionFactory>(); // 2. Define an agent with system prompts and tools var definition = new AgentDefinition("assistant", [ AgentFeature.Create(assembly => { assembly.Prompts.AddSystem("You are a helpful assistant."); assembly.Tools.Add(DelegateTool.Create("get_time", () => DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToString("O"))); }) ]); // 3. Create a session and run turns await using var session = sessionFactory.CreateSession("session-1", definition); var turn = await session.InvokeAsync([AgentMessage.FromText("user", "What time is it in UTC?")]); foreach (var message in turn.Output) { Console.WriteLine(message.Content); } Package Ecosystem Matrix Install only the modules your workload needs: Package Purpose MyAgents.Core Core interfaces (IAgent, IAgentSession, ITool, AgentDefinition, messages). MyAgents.Runtime.Chat Provider-neutral execution runtime using Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient. MyAgents.Generators Roslyn incremental source generator for zero-reflection [AgentTool] code emission. MyAgents.Runtime.Workers Long-running durable worker host with lease heartbeats and idempotency. MyAgents.Runtime.Workers.Sqlite SQLite backend for persistent durable runs. MyAgents.Memory SIMD vector store, BM25 inverted index, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, document readers. MyAgents.Mcp Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool integration over stdio and HTTP/SSE. MyAgents.Agents Subagent dispatching, group chats, token cost accounting, and model tier routing. MyAgents.Testing Deterministic in-memory test agents and session runtimes.
